title: Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho Discusses Computer Vision for Smart Agriculture in Telkom University Purwokerto Webinar

body:
**21 November 2026.** The utilization of artificial intelligence and Computer Vision to understand plant conditions became the focus of the Socio-Informatics and Professional Development Webinar organized by the Undergraduate Information Technology Study Program, Telkom University Purwokerto, Saturday (21/11). The event themed "AI for Sustainable Agriculture: The Role of Computer Vision in Realizing Smart Agriculture" featured Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho from the Department of Agricultural Engineering and Biosystems, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada, as speaker.

The webinar was conducted online via Zoom Meeting and attended by 225 participants. The event was opened by Nenen Isnaeni, representing the Head of the Information Technology Study Program. This forum served as a learning space to connect Information Technology competencies with the needs of agricultural technology development.

The material was structured beginning from the context of tropical agriculture and the relationship between water, plants, and the environment, followed by precision agriculture, smart farming, and the fundamentals of image processing. This approach placed the understanding of plants as the foundation for designing observation and data-based analysis systems.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1179-1-image-27-1030x620.webp)

One example presented was the use of thermal imagery to study plant water conditions. This example connected temperature measurement, image processing, and environmental information with the need for plant monitoring. The approach provided context for students to understand the relationship between data recorded by devices and the biological conditions being observed.

The discussion session revealed participants' interest in technology application under field conditions. One question addressed the design of monitoring for outdoor chili cultivation using an ESP32 camera connected to a mobile application, including operational challenges during the rainy season. Another question highlighted the mapping of environmental conditions, soil, and water availability.

The relationship between technology and plant physiology also became a focal point of discussion. Participants asked about the connection between water availability in soil, absorption by roots, water transport to leaves, and water release through stomata. Other participants raised the question of how to ensure that AI analysis results align with plant biological conditions, in addition to meeting computational performance measures.

System reliability also emerged through questions regarding transmission delays and data loss from sensors in thermal imagery monitoring. Meanwhile, questions about strawberry disease detection research in greenhouses led to determining the scope of Computer Vision research, from model development to its integration with IoT or robotics.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1179-2-image-28-1030x668.webp)

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1179-3-image-29-1030x600.webp)

The variety of questions demonstrated the need to bring together algorithm development with understanding of biosystems, device design, and data quality. For Information Technology students, agricultural problems provide a field of study that demands interdisciplinary work and clear establishment of research objectives.

Through this forum, learning about AI and Computer Vision was connected with agricultural problems that are closely related to user needs. The material and discussions can serve as resources for participants to formulate research ideas that consider plant conditions, the environment of use, and ways to evaluate developed technology.

This activity aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly **SDG 4: Quality Education**, through learning digital skills and understanding technology for sustainable development. The introduction of AI, Computer Vision, and sensing is also relevant to **SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure**, as preparation for developing agricultural technology research ideas and innovations. Meanwhile, the discussion of monitoring plant water conditions and cultivation environment has thematic connections with **SDG 2: Zero Hunger**, particularly sustainable agriculture. These connections lie within the scope of education and technology introduction discussed in the webinar.

original.body:
**21 November 2026.** Pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan dan Computer Vision untuk memahami kondisi tanaman menjadi fokus Webinar Sosio Informatik dan Keprofesian yang diselenggarakan Program Studi S1 Teknik Informatika, Telkom University Purwokerto, Sabtu (21/11). Kegiatan bertema “AI for Sustainable Agriculture: Peran Computer Vision dalam Mewujudkan Pertanian Cerdas” ini menghadirkan Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho dari Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada, sebagai narasumber.

Webinar dilaksanakan secara daring melalui Zoom Meeting dan diikuti 225 peserta. Kegiatan dibuka oleh Nenen Isnaeni yang hadir mewakili Ketua Program Studi Teknik Informatika. Forum ini menjadi ruang pembelajaran untuk menghubungkan kompetensi Informatika dengan kebutuhan pengembangan teknologi pertanian.

Materi disusun mulai dari konteks pertanian tropis dan hubungan air, tanaman, serta lingkungan, kemudian berlanjut pada pertanian presisi, smart farming, dan dasar pengolahan citra. Alur tersebut menempatkan pemahaman terhadap tanaman sebagai landasan untuk merancang sistem pengamatan dan analisis berbasis data.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1179-1-image-27-1030x620.webp)

Salah satu contoh yang diangkat dalam bahan paparan adalah penggunaan citra termal untuk mempelajari kondisi air tanaman. Contoh ini menghubungkan pengukuran suhu, pengolahan citra, dan informasi lingkungan dengan kebutuhan pemantauan tanaman. Pendekatan tersebut memberi konteks bagi mahasiswa untuk memahami hubungan antara data yang direkam perangkat dan kondisi biologis yang hendak diamati.

Sesi diskusi memperlihatkan perhatian peserta terhadap penerapan teknologi dalam kondisi lapangan. Salah satu pertanyaan membahas rancangan pemantauan pada pertanaman cabai di luar ruangan menggunakan kamera ESP32 yang terhubung dengan aplikasi seluler, termasuk tantangan pengoperasian saat musim hujan. Pertanyaan lain menyoroti pemetaan kondisi lingkungan, tanah, dan ketersediaan air.

Hubungan antara teknologi dan fisiologi tanaman juga menjadi pokok pertanyaan. Peserta menanyakan keterkaitan ketersediaan air di dalam tanah, penyerapan oleh akar, transportasi air menuju daun, dan pelepasan air melalui stomata. Peserta lainnya mengangkat persoalan bagaimana memastikan hasil analisis AI sesuai dengan kondisi biologis tanaman, selain memenuhi ukuran kinerja komputasi.

Aspek keandalan sistem turut muncul melalui pertanyaan mengenai keterlambatan pengiriman dan kehilangan data sensor pada pemantauan berbasis citra termal. Sementara itu, pertanyaan tentang penelitian deteksi penyakit stroberi di greenhouse mengarah pada penentuan ruang lingkup penelitian Computer Vision, mulai dari pengembangan model hingga integrasinya dengan IoT atau robotika.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1179-2-image-28-1030x668.webp)

![](/brand/uploads/notes/1179-3-image-29-1030x600.webp)

Ragam pertanyaan tersebut menunjukkan kebutuhan untuk mempertemukan pengembangan algoritma dengan pemahaman biosistem, rancangan perangkat, dan mutu data. Bagi mahasiswa Informatika, persoalan pertanian menyediakan ruang kajian yang menuntut kerja lintas disiplin serta penetapan tujuan penelitian yang jelas.

Melalui forum ini, pembelajaran AI dan Computer Vision dihubungkan dengan persoalan pertanian yang dekat dengan kebutuhan pengguna. Materi dan diskusi dapat menjadi bahan bagi peserta untuk merumuskan gagasan penelitian yang mempertimbangkan kondisi tanaman, lingkungan penggunaan, serta cara mengevaluasi teknologi yang dikembangkan.

Kegiatan ini sejalan dengan Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan (Sustainable Development Goals/SDGs), terutama **SDG 4: Pendidikan Berkualitas**, melalui pembelajaran keterampilan digital dan pemahaman teknologi untuk pembangunan berkelanjutan. Pengenalan AI, Computer Vision, dan sensing juga relevan dengan **SDG 9: Industri, Inovasi, dan Infrastruktur**, sebagai bekal pengembangan gagasan riset dan inovasi teknologi pertanian. Adapun pembahasan pemantauan kondisi air tanaman dan lingkungan budidaya memiliki keterkaitan tematik dengan **SDG 2: Tanpa Kelaparan**, khususnya pertanian berkelanjutan. Keterkaitan tersebut berada pada lingkup edukasi dan pengenalan teknologi yang dibahas dalam webinar.
